questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Choosing Lucerne, Switzerland as a study destination for law students hinges on several pivotal factors. First and foremost, the academic reputation and excellence of the law programs play a pivotal role. Lucerne's universities should offer a strong foundation in legal education, thereby fostering a promising legal career. Also, I thought it would be great to train my German language skills as well as English.
Moreover, the local and cultural ambiance of Lucerne are crucial; its breathtaking landscapes and rich cultural heritage offer an environment that complements your academic journey. This picturesque setting provides opportunities for extracurricular engagement and networking, which can be invaluable in the legal field. I also thought it would be fantastic to meet new people and peers, and get to know other cultures as well, from countries all over the world. And the academic environment is great. 
Additionally, the presence of internship and job opportunities within or near Lucerne is a decisive factor. Gaining practical experience while studying is indispensable for law students, facilitating a smoother transition into the legal profession post-graduation. In summary, the choice of Lucerne as a study destination for law students is a multifaceted decision, encompassing academic quality, language proficiency, cultural appeal, and career prospects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy I would say. The international team at the University made it easy and they were great at communicating and making events for the new students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Events and contact info. I never felt "alone" with anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were just great and very sweet!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were one housing organisation. Not owned by the University, but they had a collaboration. It was the only option.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a canteen. The food was good and everything was plant-based, also reasonably priced. Around 75-100 DKK for a lunch (that is cheap for Switzerland).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Lucerne is very difficult and very expensive to live in. Housing on your own is VERY difficult to find. So The Student Mentor Organisation was pretty much the only available option. I found it to be pretty expensive for what you got. It was very cold temperature wise during winter and even spring, as my room was not on the sunny side of the building, and the boss at the place were very conservative and stubborn in their behaviour. Several of us encountered problems with them, and it is frankly impossible to get out of the housing contract or get your money back if you are not satisfied. They ask you to pay around 1000 francs before you even move in and will not give it back to you if you choose to live somewhere else. You live with other full-time students – not the exchange students and you can do nothing about it. They already live there when you move in. I arrived at a bit of greasy place with dust in the corners and flies in the sink. So if you are stuck in a bad apartment and do not like the rommates, that is just unfortunate. Also, men and women share the same bath and toilet. You live five people in the same apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing is not the best.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty straight-forward I would say.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international team at the university in their office or via mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes you wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just listen to the international team at the university and read the info (mails, folders etc.) they give you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was in the middle – not too easy, not too hard. But some of the courses are mandatory! The Swiss people are much more concerned about this than UPCH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UPCH is harder.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Copyright in the Digital Age, Internet Law, Introduction to Swiss Law, Introduction to the Common Law System, Law and Economics and Negotiating and Drafting International Commercial Contracts.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Swiss Law as this course is both out of campus and at the campus. When out of campus, you go to monuments, and you get a little food and background info about Switzerland. But this is only in the beginning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation was really expensive, and food as well. I felt like food sometimes was almost double of the Danish prices. My food budget was way too low put and I needed to use almost all of my savings on just living okay. I never ate out as it was ridiculously expensive. There was an indian restaurant close to our University and it was 27 francs for a butter chicken. It is around 200 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and transportation. Generally, the prices felt around 20-30 % higher and food sometimes 50 % higher than DKK. Do not go here if you do not like to spend money! I was kind of jealous of some of my peers that went to Italy and Spain as they ate out every night while all I got was homecooked rice and pasta. We ate out sometimes but mainly pizza and kebab.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It costed money to do the more advanced acitivities and go on camps etc. But there were dance lessons as well as other "basic" activities and a lowkey gym at the University for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different kinds within what you normally would expect. Football, volleyball, dance, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The dance lessons was pretty fun. I did not try more than those as I also had to study and do a lot of other things.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them to travel the country. A travel pass for a month cost around 2500 DKK. It is very expensive but the transportation is good and it has beautiful views. Participate in the student environment such as the ESN and make many new friends. Go out and explore the night life as well and bring the big wallet as drinks are pretty costly ;-)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was more or less easy. The Swiss are more conservative people who likes they "private space", but they are not too far away from Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the activities around you. Both through the University and the ESN-programme. If you live at the associated student organisation's campus, you will also make friends if you live with the other people in a shared flat. For the local students it is more hard, as they are not as willing to be with you as the international students. But you can always meet some at the campus or just talk to them at the University, even though that might be a little odd. Especially since they speak Swiss German.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swiss are more closed people and they do not socialize with foreign people that much. When going out, they stay a lot in their own groups, people say. Also, they are not so used to date a lot, they stick with one partner and are more loyal I would say. Danes are more free and like to speak with people, especially when drunk.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hmmm. I think I appreciated the cultural aspects about the nature the most. A big part of Swiss culture is just being, wandering and skiing in the Alps. I liked that compared to flat Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be yourself but also be curious about other people. 
2) Go out, have fun and enjoy your time. Do not worry too much about school and grades, this is the time of your life! 3) Bring a big wallet and do not look too much at the prices. Money comes and goes, memories stay forever.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare as much as you can in advance and read the e-mails you get from both Univeristy of Lucerne and University of Copenhagen. And also, bring warm clothes but do not expect you can pack everything because that is impossible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The memories to be honest. And the relationship with myself – I got to know myself much better and I realised how beautiful the world is. Coming from the pandemic into this was really rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The social aspects and the money-aspect. It was hard to socialize 24/7 almost. At the end, I spent much more time alone and it was really nice. I made some local friends and spent time with them also instead of ONLY being in the bubble of the exchange students. Also, the money-aspects was rough. I felt broke all the time. Also my friend from Denmark, who was also there on an exchange, thought the same. She was kind of sad at times about it. Because we could not go out and eat, spend too much on drinks etc. We really had to watch our money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just enjoy it and have fun. Do not think too much about small details. Socialize but also spend time alone to experience and travel.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
